_comment: MERGED 2026-09-02: this is a superset, not a replacement. The first 36 entries (g01-g36 ids) are the original session-store-mined rebuild - every one traces to a real ~/.copilot/session-store.db user message verified as an exact substring at a cited (session_id, turn_index), and every target page was verified by reading it, never by running a search and recording the result. See provenance.json for the verbatim quote, session id, turn index and timestamp on each - provenance_type 'session'. That set previously measured paraphrase Recall@20 54.5%->81.8% and overall 81.5%->92.6% with NO retrieval code change, the cleanest available proof that the prior synthetic paraphrase class (not this one) was the defect, not the retrieval system. Three real defects were caught and fixed while building it: g05's expect_facts was a fabricated composite absent from memory.db (replaced with real fact id=38); g11/g23 had mojibake U+FFFD where the DB has an em dash (byte-corrected); g21's second target is a builder-truncated filename stem (the page title reads '...pitches are wrong', the file on disk ends '...obvious pi.md'). The remaining 21 entries (ids gcc-*/cu-*/mh-*) are owner-curated additions layered on top per the owner's explicit priority domains (GCC product availability: Agent P3, Copilot Studio, Dev Box; GCC models/access: ZDR, Claude/Anthropic, Azure Government vs GCC, GCC Entra enclave vs commercial; Content Understanding: closed model list, billing meters, analyzer-vs-model cost lever, prebuilt-read meter, checkbox defect, legal-doc RAG routing, and the Azure-Government-vs-M365-GCC availability nuance) plus the owner's explicit GitHub-Copilot local/paraphrase pair. These have no verbatim session-store source; provenance.json marks them provenance_type 'owner-curated' rather than fabricating a session citation. Ground truth for every curated entry was still established by reading the target page in full. 8 curated queries that were near-duplicates of an existing harvested query (same page, same fact, materially the same question) were pruned as padding rather than kept - their verified expect_facts/expect_pages were folded into the harvested entry they duplicated instead of being lost: gcc-agent365 (dup of g13) and gcc-fabric (dup of g12) folded their fact into g12/g13; gcc-teamsphone (dup of g28); cu-poc (exact-text dup of g06); gcc-claude-datazone (near-dup of g30, folded its two extra expect_pages into g30); cu-customweights-trap (near-dup of g26, folded its fact into g26); gcc-voicemai-cost (near-dup of g32, folded its fact into g32); mh-devbox-frontline (near-dup of g23, same Dev Box/Frontline two-page synthesis). Class is assigned honestly per wording-vs-page-vocabulary throughout, never padded to hit a minimum - several paraphrase/multihop entries are deliberately the 'GCC uses commercial Azure, not Azure Government' trap (a retrieval system returning 'not available in GCC' for an Azure service, or missing the reverse Power Platform exception which genuinely runs on Azure Government, is confidently wrong), and the GitHub Copilot pair is the deliberate CONTRAST case: it is a SaaS product where 'not available in GCC' is genuinely true but incomplete (GitHub Copilot Enterprise + US data residency + FedRAMP model restrictions is a real supported path) - a system that pattern-matches 'GCC -> unavailable' uniformly fails this case exactly where it succeeds on the Azure-service traps. expect_pages values are vault page stems, resolved the same way as wiki/vault_mcp.py:_resolve(). expect_facts are populated only where the exact string was verified to round-trip against facts.content in memory.db immediately before this file was written; everything else is left []. Excludes '10-Synthesis/Retrieval v4 Phase 3 impact on GCC and Content Understanding litmus tests' (self-authored by this session's own agents).

expect_facts: SAIF claims Content Understanding COST-OPTIMIZATION insight (from Vijay's April 25 2026 email to rambal@saif.com, thread 'Analyzer in CU for Layout + Schema'): Two cost levers proven in the PoC -> (1) GPT-4.1-mini vs GPT-4.1 = ~80% cheaper tokens (~ per 8K-image batch on 4.1 -> ~-800 on mini); (2) BIGGEST lever: drop the LLM entirely by switching analyzer from prebuilt-documentFields (LLM-based, forced full GPT-4.1 at / per 1M tokens, no mini support) to prebuilt-read (pure OCR) or prebuilt-layout (OCR+tables) = NO LLM tokens = projected ~98-99% cost reduction. Root cause: prebuilt-documentFields is a utility analyzer that doesn't support mini and runs everything at full GPT-4.1 rates. Direction Vijay recommended: OCR-only field extraction (prebuilt-read/layout) or a custom analyzer for claim docs, especially when only markdown/text+fields are needed (no generative grounding). Baseline observed: 8K images ~=  (~37-40 cents/image on the LLM run) vs expected 3-5 cents/image. This reduction ladder (LLM full 100 / mini 20 / OCR-only ~1.5) is now the cost slide in the SAIF AI Briefing deck.
